questions.prompt: Why do you think that, since 1661, there have been so few changes made to these positions?
questions.passage: In 1661, King Louis XIV of France founded a Royal Academy of Dancing. The Academy devised rules for the correct ballet steps, based on five main positions of the feet. The positions were planned to give a balance to any position of the body. To this day there have been only a few minor changes made to these positions.
questions.markingGuide: Accept answers stating the positions were already well-designed/effective — they gave good balance to the body — so there was little need to change them, e.g. 'because they worked well/gave good balance so they didn't need changing'. Reject answers that don't address why the positions themselves have endured (e.g. attributing it only to the king's authority/rules without addressing the balance/effectiveness reasoning given in the text).

questions.prompt: Do you think Shepherd's Purse is commonly grown by gardeners? Why do you say that?
questions.passage: Shepherd's Purse is a herb that is a member of the mustard family. It has a tap root and jagged edged leaves. The flowers grow at the ends of the slender stems. They are small, white and rather delicate. Commonly seen growing in wastelands and fields everywhere, it is often used in herbal medicine. It is, however, regarded as a curse in most gardens.
questions.markingGuide: Accept 'No' with evidence that it is 'regarded as a curse in most gardens' and grows wild in 'wastelands and fields' rather than being deliberately planted. Reject 'Yes' or answers without this evidence.

questions.prompt: Who do you think picked the chocolate chips out of the biscuits? Why do you say that?
questions.passage:
"Who picked the chocolate chips out of these biscuits?" she demanded to know. Mum was standing by the trays of newly baked biscuits that had been left to cool on the kitchen bench.

When it came to the extras in the food division, David preferred an apple or a sandwich. He would eat only small amounts of sugary food. Bill loved biscuits, cakes and pastries. He was an athlete and said he needed the fuel. Peter would eat anything that he could. He was only three years old and needed a lot of looking after.

Bill said it wasn't fair to accuse him. He'd just got back from a long run. Peter, rubbing his hands on his sweatshirt, said "Not me!" David shrugged his shoulders as if to say "As if!"
questions.markingGuide: Accept 'David' with evidence that he prefers less sugary food (apple/sandwich) and only eats small amounts of sugary food, and his guilty body language ('shrugged his shoulders as if to say "As if!"' — a denial that reads as suspicious). Reject 'Bill' or 'Peter' as the primary answer, since Bill has an alibi (just finished a run) and Peter is too young/unlikely to selectively remove chips.

questions.prompt: Is the Empire State Building the tallest building in the world? Why do you say that?
questions.passage:
Looking up at all the skyscrapers, Angela instructed Kay to "Go into Alf's news agency over there and buy a map of the city."

She looked around for a seat. "It's the only way we'll ever find it. I know it's around here somewhere. When King Kong climbed up it in the original movie, it was the tallest building in the world."

Kay crossed the road and disappeared through the dark doorway. A few minutes later she came out and handed the map to Angela who opened it, spreading it out on her knees.

The two friends had arrived for their short holiday in New York and had set out on foot to see as much as they could.

Angela clicked her tongue and said, "Oh!" softly, as if to herself. "Well, it's quite a few blocks from here. Quite a walk. Here, look."

Kay studied the map. She found where they were at the moment and traced a path to their destination with her eyes. She looked back at the starting point.

"Well," she said cheerfully, looking down at her feet. "It's OK, I'm wearing the right shoes." "I've just had a thought," she said. "I could have saved six dollars by just asking Alf."

After a short silence, during which Angela folded the map carefully placing the segment that they would need on the outside, she had another thought.

"I think it's amazing that we couldn't find the Empire State Building."
questions.markingGuide: Accept 'No' with evidence that the text specifies it 'was' the tallest 'in the original [King Kong] movie' (past tense, i.e. no longer true today) — implying other buildings have since been built taller. Reject 'Yes' or an answer without this reasoning.
